'''Alex Biryukov''' ({{Langx|he|אלכס ביריוקוב}}) is a [[cryptographer]], currently a full professor at the [[University of Luxembourg]].

==Biography==
His notable work includes the design of the [[stream cipher]] [[LEX (cipher)|LEX]], as well as the [[cryptanalysis]] of numerous [[cryptographic primitive]]s. In 1998, he developed [[impossible differential cryptanalysis]] together with [[Eli Biham]] and [[Adi Shamir]].<ref>{{ Cite journal | author = Bruce Schneier | title = Impossible Cryptanalysis and Skipjack | journal = Crypto-Gram Newsletter | date = 15 September 1998 | url = http://www.schneier.com/crypto-gram-9809.html#impossible }}</ref> In 1999, he developed the [[slide attack]] together with [[David A. Wagner|David Wagner]]. In 2009 he developed, together with [[Dmitry Khovratovich]], the first cryptanalytic attack on full-round [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]]-192 and AES-256 that is faster than a [[brute-force attack]].<ref>{{cite web | author = Alex Biryukov | author2 = Dmitry Khovratovich | author2-link = Dmitry Khovratovich | title = Related-key Cryptanalysis of the Full AES-192 and AES-256 | date = 28 June 2009 | url = http://eprint.iacr.org/2009/317.pdf | accessdate = 3 July 2009}}</ref> In 2015 he developed the [[Argon2]] [[key derivation function]] with Daniel Dinu and Dmitry Khovratovich.<ref>{{cite web | author = Alex Biryukov | author2 = Daniel Dinu | author3 = Dmitry Khovratovich | title = Argon2: the memory-hard function for password hashing and other applications | date = 26 December 2015 | url = https://password-hashing.net/argon2-specs.pdf }}</ref>
Since 1994 Alex Biryukov is a member of the [[International Association for Cryptologic Research]].
